member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltResultDocument.CdataSectionElements
member.summary: The cdata-section-elements serialization attribute: a whitespace-separated list of element QNames whose text content is serialized inside <![CDATA[…]]>. Stored as an AVT because it is an attribute value template on xsl:result-document (result-document-0401). Evaluated at runtime, split on whitespace and resolved to QNames against ; the effective set is the union with the matched xsl:output declaration's cdata-section-elements (result-document-0240).

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltResultDocument.ParameterDocument
member.summary: The parameter-document serialization attribute (an AVT; XSLT 3.0 §27.1). References an external output:serialization-parameters document whose parameters (notably method) and inline character maps supplement this result-document's serialization. Resolved and loaded at runtime because the URI may reference variables (insn/result-document/result-document-1406 uses "{$o}-params.xml"). Values set directly on xsl:result-document take precedence over the parameter document per §27.1.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltWithParam
member.summary: xsl:with-param in apply-templates or call-template.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltWithParam.FromRuntimeOptions
member.summary: True when this parameter came from a RUNTIME option rather than a literal xsl:with-param in a stylesheet — today, fn:transform's template-params and tunnel-params.
member.remarks:
XTSE0680 — "parameter not declared in the called template" — is a STATIC error: it is about what an author wrote next to an xsl:call-template, and the engine raises it in CallTemplateAsync. A runtime map is different: fn:transform supplies template-params without knowing which parameters the chosen initial template declares, and values for parameters it does not declare are simply ignored.
Without this distinction, one undeclared entry aborts the whole transform. XSpec passes its param-items to whichever template a scenario names, so a single scenario whose template does not declare it terminated the entire suite.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltWithParam.RuntimeValue
member.summary: A value supplied DIRECTLY, rather than one to be produced by evaluating or . Only meaningful when is true.
member.remarks: fn:transform's template-params and tunnel-params already hold real XDM values — nodes, sequences, maps, arrays — and there is nothing to evaluate. Routing them through a synthesised Select expression meant first turning each value into a literal, and no literal can express a node: everything that was not a string, number or boolean was flattened with ToString(). A node-valued parameter arrived as a string, and the first axis step on it raised XPTY0020.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltWithParam.HasRuntimeValue
member.summary: True when holds the parameter's value. Distinct from testing the value for null, because null IS a value here — the empty sequence.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltMergeSource.Streamable
member.summary: XSLT 3.0 streaming hint: streamable="yes" on xsl:merge-source. Today the engine accepts and parses the attribute but executes the merge non-streaming (each source is fully materialized before K-way merge runs). Reserved for future XmlReader-driven incremental merge — when the source is paired with for-each-source URIs, a streamable runtime would open each URI as XmlReader and pull items one at a time through the K-way merge, keeping the watermark to N items rather than the full N×size sequences.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltStylesheet.AbstractVariableNames
member.summary: Names of variables from used packages that remain abstract (not overridden with a concrete definition). A global variable of the used package that references one of these has no evaluable value, so it must be deferred (bound lazily) rather than eagerly evaluated; evaluating it — i.e. actually referencing it — is XTDE3052. (accept-042/043: an unreferenced public proxy over an abstract variable must not fail.)

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltStylesheet.PackageLocalShadowVariables
member.summary: Package-local global variables that could not take the principal QName-keyed slot because a same-named global from another package already claimed it. Each is stamped with its owning package () and resolved per calling package at runtime, so a diamond override / different-version import (use-package-175 / use-package-176) sees each package's own value rather than one shared binding. Empty for non-package stylesheets.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltStylesheet.PackagePrivateGlobals
member.summary: Global variables/parameters that a used package declares WITHOUT exposing across the xsl:use-package boundary (private — explicitly, or by the package default). Each maps the component's QName to its owning used package. Such a component is merged (so the used package's own components may still reference it) but must not be resolvable from the using package: a reference from any other package raises XPST0008 (use-package-006 / use-package-007). Empty for non-package stylesheets.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltStylesheet.VisibleAcrossPackageBoundary(System.String)
member.summary: A global variable of a used package is visible across the xsl:use-package boundary only when its visibility is EXPLICITLY public, final, or abstract (xsl:expose sets directly instead). A variable whose visibility merely defaulted to public — the parser's workaround so plain xsl:import/xsl:include modules stay mutually visible — is private under xsl:package and must not leak across the boundary. Callers pass (the raw attribute string, null when absent).

member.summary: Symbolic names (kind, name, arity) of public/final components exposed by packages referenced via xsl:use-package. A component declared in the using package (outside xsl:override) whose symbolic name matches one of these is a static error (XTSE3050). Kinds: "V" variable/param, "F" function, "M" mode.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltStylesheet.LocalComponentSymbols
member.summary: Symbolic names (kind, name, arity) of components declared locally in this package at the top level (not inside xsl:override, not merged from a used package). Checked against for XTSE3050.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltStylesheet.AcceptedComponentSymbols
member.summary: Symbolic names (kind, name, arity) of components that have become visible (accepted, not hidden) components of THIS package from an xsl:use-package. Each xsl:use-package is a distinct package instance, so two such contributions of the same symbolic name — whether from two different used packages (decl/accept-020) or the same package reached by two routes in a diamond (decl/package-022err) — are two distinct components with the same name and are a static error (XTSE3050), unless one is resolved by xsl:override. Populated per use-package and propagated across xsl:include boundaries (MergeStylesheet) so a conflict spanning two included modules is detected. Kinds: "T" template, "V" variable, "F" function, "A" attribute-set, "M" mode.

member.summary: The library package (used via xsl:use-package) that declared this global variable. Global variables are LOCAL to their declaring package (XSLT 3.0 §3.6): a reference from a component resolves the variable as seen by THAT component's package. When two packages contribute a same-named global with different values (diamond override or different used versions), only one can occupy the principal QName-keyed slot; the other is recorded as a package-local shadow and resolved per calling package (use-package-175 / use-package-176). Captured at the boundary so a later xsl:accept that lowers the component to private keeps it usable inside the using package (a provided-then-accepted-private global is still visible), while a component the used package never exposed stays invisible to any other package (use-package-006 / use-package-007). member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltContext.SequencePredicateEvaluator
member.summary: Evaluates a chain of predicates against a node with true XPath filter semantics. Given the node being tested, the step's predicate list, its node test, and the optional descendant-axis ancestor, this builds the candidate sequence the node belongs to (in document order) and applies each predicate to the sequence that survived the earlier predicates — so position()/last() inside a later predicate are relative to the re-indexed survivors. Returns true iff the node is in the final filtered sequence. Used for patterns with two or more predicates such as x[(position() mod 2)=1][position() > 3]; single-predicate steps keep the cheaper path. Null when no sequence-aware evaluator is wired (e.g. the streaming accumulator match context), in which case the caller falls back to per-node predicate evaluation.

member.summary: XSLT 3.0 §19.6/§19.7 usage of the matched context item . by the for-each BODY — the second usage axis, orthogonal to (which is the for-each RESULT's usage by its enclosing construct). Stamped by the scanner via . Defaults to (deliver the node) — the legacy default for subscriptions that do not atomize their select; only a data()-wrapped select yields Absorption.

member.summary: The XSLT 3.0 §19.6/§19.7 operand usage of this for-each's RESULT — the role the enclosing construct imposes on the items the body emits. when the for-each sits directly in element/complex content (§5.7.1: constructed nodes are transmitted, so a document/element node breaks the atomic run and adjacent nodes are NOT space-separated); (the default, preserving legacy behavior) when the result is captured into a variable and later atomized (§5.7.2: space-separated). member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.ForEachSubscription.InlineDriven
member.summary: True when the for-each is lexically nested inside output construction (an LRE, xsl:element, xsl:copy, xsl:if, xsl:choose) rather than being a bare top-of-body instruction. member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.ForEachSubscription.IsInspectionOnly
member.summary: Non-consuming dispatch (Group B): the matched node's body inspects ancestors/ancestor-or-self/parent/self/attributes only (plus atomize and set-ops over those) — it never descends into the matched node's subtree. The processor dispatches the body per match against an ancestor-synthesized snapshot WITHOUT materializing/skipping the subtree, so the forward pass continues into descendants where deeper //X matches still fire. Registered ONLY when the body is provably inspection-only (BodyConsumptionDetector.Consumes == false) — the soundness guard.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.ForEachSubscription.Outermost
member.summary: From outermost(...): a match is skipped when an ancestor on the live stack also matches the subscription's pattern (decided immediately from the ancestor stack — no buffering). For a bare descendant path (//X) this is false and every match dispatches.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.ForEachSubscription.ConsumingOutermost
member.summary:
Consuming outermost(//X) dispatch: the for-each select is outermost(//X) over a descendant-axis path but the body is NOT inspection-only — it atomizes the bare context item . (needs the matched leaf's own text value), so the empty-children inspection snapshot would be wrong. Because outermost matches never nest, materialize-and-skip is sound: the consuming dispatch materializes the matched subtree (capturing its text), synthesizes the ancestor chain (so ../@CAT / ancestor:: resolve), and executes the body against that snapshot. Registered by TryRegisterInspectionForEach when the inspection-only gate fails but the select is outermost; the consuming dispatch block honors the ancestor-dedup for these (unlike plain child-axis consuming subscriptions, which never nest by construction).
This carries a descendant-axis (**), which the child-axis-only TryBuildPathMatcher gate rejects — hence it is registered directly rather than via the ordinary consuming path.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.ForEachSubscription.GateCondition
member.summary: Runtime branch-gate for a conditional for-each select for-each select="if(C) then T else E" where the condition C is GROUNDED (motionless — a variable / constant, evaluated once against the live scope) and exactly ONE branch is a streamable path while the OTHER is the empty sequence (). This subscription carries the streamable branch's path; it fires ONLY when the gate is open. The gate is open when the effective boolean value of equals — i.e. when the condition selects the streamable branch. If it selects the empty branch, the subscription is skipped entirely (nothing is iterated), which is the exact and sound behaviour because the other branch is (). null = no gate (unconditional subscription). member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.ForEachSubscription.GateFiresWhenConditionTrue

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.HttpImportPreloader
member.summary: Walks an XSLT module's xsl:import / xsl:include graph asynchronously, fetching every HTTP/HTTPS-resolved href and storing it in . Called from LoadStylesheetAsync BEFORE the synchronous parser runs, so the parser's import resolver always finds HTTP modules in the cache and never invokes the sync-blocking HttpResourceLoader.GetStringSync path that breaks on WASM (single-threaded runtime can't wait on monitors).
member.remarks: Best-effort: any fetch failure is swallowed so the synchronous parser surfaces the canonical XTSE0165 error with full context (the parser already handles cache miss by attempting the sync HTTP fetch on non-browser runtimes, and producing a clear "preload required" exception on browser runtimes).

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.HttpResourceLoader
member.summary: Fetches stylesheet modules and similar text resources over HTTP/HTTPS.

remarks.para: XSLT 3.0 doesn't restrict the scheme of xsl:include/xsl:import hrefs — any URI is fair game. The parser resolves the href against the entry stylesheet's base URI; when that resolves to http:// or https://, this helper performs the fetch.

The parser is synchronous, so this exposes a sync-blocking that runs the async call to completion. Stylesheet imports are infrequent (compile-time only) and modest in size, so blocking the calling thread here is acceptable.

A single static with a 30-second timeout is reused across the process to amortize handshake/connection cost. The timeout is conservative — a stylesheet over 30 s of network is almost certainly a misconfiguration that the user will want to surface as an error rather than have hang the build.

Sandboxing remains the caller's responsibility: ResourcePolicy is consulted before this helper is invoked, so a configured policy can deny HTTP imports entirely or restrict them to specific hosts/path prefixes.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.HttpResourceLoader.GetStringSync(System.Uri)
member.summary: Fetches the resource at as a string. Blocks the calling thread until the request completes.
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails (network error, non-success status, timeout). Wrapping in IOException lets the existing parser catch (IOException) path produce the standard XTSE0165 error.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.AnnotationPopulator
member.summary: Activates the side-table by classifying a set of independently-classifiable units (template bodies, streamable constructs) with a root streaming context and caching each unit's composed . This makes unit-level posture queryable without re-running the classifier — the substrate posture-driven consumers (SP-B onward) build on.
member.remarks: Scope: annotation is at the granularity of whole classifiable units. Per-node compositional annotation (where a child's streaming context differs from the unit root) is deferred to the first consumer (SP-B): composes a unit's posture by recursing internally and does not surface per-child contexts, so the consuming context is what defines a correct per-node annotation.

member.summary: The streaming environment in which an expression is classified: the posture of the context item and whether that context item is live-streamed.
member.param: The posture of the context item (.) at this point, per XSLT 3.0 §19.8.2. For a streamed source-document body or a matched streaming template the context item is ; for a grounded/materialised context it is .
Whether the context item is a live-streamed node. When false the whole expression is grounded regardless of navigation (nothing streamed to consume).

In-scope variable bindings (name → the of the bound expression), accumulated as a sequence-constructor body or FLWOR clause list is walked. A VariableReference to a name present here resolves to that recorded posture instead of the conservative context-posture approximation. null means no bindings are in scope. member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier
member.summary: Compositional streamability classifier for the XPath/XQuery expression language, implementing the XSLT 3.0 §19.8 (Streamability) posture/sweep composition rules.

remarks.para: This is a shadow component (Task 0.3): it is pure analysis, wired into nothing and deleting nothing. It computes the of an expression given the posture of its context item, exactly as §19.8 describes:

item.description: Posture (§19.1) — where the result nodes sit relative to the streamed context (grounded / striding / crawling / climbing / roaming).
Sweep (§19.1) — whether evaluating the expression advances the stream (motionless / consuming / free-ranging).

remarks.para: Any expression kind not yet modelled is conservatively classified (Roaming, FreeRanging) — i.e. NOT guaranteed streamable — so nothing is silently mis-accepted. Those cases are marked with // TODO.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.Classify(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: Computes the composed of in the streaming environment , per XSLT 3.0 §19.8.
member.param: The expression to classify.
The streaming context (context-item posture and streamed-scope flag).
member.returns: The composed posture and sweep of the expression's result.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifyStep(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.StepExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: Classifies a single axis step applied to an operand of posture , per the §19.8.8 axis/posture composition rules.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifyIfExpression(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.IfExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: §19.8: if (T) then E1 else E2. Result posture = WIDEN(posture(E1), posture(E2)); result sweep = COMBINE(sweep(T), sweep(E1), sweep(E2)). A free-ranging test, or a branch that roams / free-ranges, propagates (mirrors the XsltIf/XsltChoose instruction arm). The XQuery-4.0 braced-if (null else) has an implicit empty-sequence else, which is grounded+motionless and absorbed by .

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifyMapConstructor(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.MapConstructor,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: §19.8.2: a constructed map { k: v, ... } is GROUNDED (a brand-new function item, detached from the stream), even though its key/value expressions may consume the streamed input. Sweep = COMBINE over every key and value expression's sweep. A non-streamable key or value propagates. Mirrors the XsltMap/XsltMapEntry instruction arm.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifyArrayConstructor(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ArrayConstructor,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: §19.8.2: a constructed array — square [ ... ] or curly array { ... } — is GROUNDED (a brand-new array item), even though its member expressions may consume the streamed input. Sweep = COMBINE over every member expression's sweep. A non-streamable member propagates. Mirrors the XsltArray/XsltArrayMember instruction arm.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifyLookup(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: §19.8.2: a map/array lookup base?key extracts a stored value from a GROUNDED map or array function item. The extracted value is grounded, motionless of its own; the sweep is the combine of the base's and (optional) key's sweeps. A non-streamable base or key propagates. The base MUST be a streamable posture (a lookup on a streamed node-set is not modelled here — it stays conservative because the base classify would not be a map/array).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifyDynamicCall(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.DynamicFunctionCallExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: §19.8: a dynamic function call fnexpr(args) is grounded ONLY when the function EXPRESSION is itself grounded (a grounded function item cannot navigate the OUTER streamed input) and every argument is streamable. Result grounded; sweep = combine of the function-expression and argument sweeps. A non-grounded function expression stays conservative (NotStreamable). This is intentionally narrower than blanket-grounding higher-order calls: it only accepts a call whose target is a grounded function item (e.g. a lookup into a grounded map: random-number-generator(.)?permute($options)).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.BindVar(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext,System.String,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture)
member.summary: Returns with variable bound to in scope (see ). Used by the xsl:variable body walk and the FLWOR let/for clause walk to make a later VariableReference resolve to the binding's posture rather than the conservative context-posture approximation.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.GroundedFrom(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: A grounded (atomic/boolean) result derived from inspecting WITHOUT atomizing it, that nonetheless propagates non-streamability: if the operand roams or is free-ranging, the whole expression is not guaranteed streamable.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.AtomizeSweep(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: The sweep contributed by ATOMIZING an operand (as a comparison / cast / arithmetic / string-value operand does). §19.8: atomizing a striding or crawling node walks its element string-value (the whole subtree) ⇒ Consuming, even if navigating to the node was itself motionless. Atomizing a climbing node (an attribute / namespace) or a grounded value reads no streamed subtree ⇒ the operand's own sweep. A free-ranging operand stays free-ranging. This is exactly what separates the streamable attribute predicate @v[xs:decimal(.) gt 0] (climbing . → motionless) from the non-streamable element predicate PAGES[. lt 1000] (striding . → consuming ⇒ the filtered sequence roams).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.Consumes(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)

M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.AllOperandsStreamable(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression},PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: True iff every operand is individually guaranteed-streamable (streamable posture AND not free-ranging). Used by absorbing/boolean functions so a roaming operand (e.g. a consuming-predicate filter) is not silently flattened to "consuming".

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.CombineSweep(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Sweep,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Sweep)
member.summary: Combines two sweeps taking the more-consuming of the two: Motionless < Consuming < FreeRanging. (§19.8: sequential composition of sweeps.)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.IsNodeCombiningExpression(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True if COMBINES multiple node sequences into one (a union / intersect / except, or a comma-sequence of ≥2 items). §19.8.8.3: navigating a further step off such a combined operand is not guaranteed streamable.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.IsForEachPopulationPosture(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture)
member.summary: The postures a for-each / iterate population (select) expression may have and still stream: STRIDING (a flat set of siblings, the classic streamable loop), GROUNDED (a materialised sequence — e.g. .//*/name() mapped to strings, or a grounded map's keys), or CLIMBING (an attribute / namespace population reachable motionlessly off the streamed element, e.g. account/transaction[@value lt 0]/@value or child::A/@id; each per-item context is an attribute/namespace whose grounded body consumes nothing forward — si-lre-A cy-001). A CRAWLING select (nested descendants, //ITEM/TITLE) is NOT streamable in a loop (si-for-each-806); roaming likewise. The body-must-be-grounded requirement (enforced by the callers) keeps a climbing per-item context from being returned as a live streamed node.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.CapturesStreamedNodes(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture)
member.summary: §19.8.2: true when is a DOWNWARD / FORWARD streamed NODE posture — Striding (children of the streamed context) or Crawling (descendants). Such a sequence is a LIVE view over the streamed input; capturing it into a grounded map/array value (or using it as a key) would require buffering the whole sub-sequence, which §19.8 forbids. Grounded (detached), Climbing (an attribute/ancestor already in hand, motionless), and atomic values are storable and return false here. This is the rule that rejects si-map-901 (map value = //AUTHOR) / sx-square-array-201 ([$g, //ITEM]) while leaving si-iterate-037's grounded-context accumulator (map:put(...,.) where . is a grounded string) streamable.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.WidenNodePosture(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture)
member.summary: Widens two node postures per §19.8.8.3: any pairing that involves descendant nesting is crawling; two striding operands compose to crawling (their node-sets may interleave).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.IsHigherOrderMapArrayFunction(System.String)
member.summary: The HIGHER-ORDER members of the map: / array: function libraries — those taking a FUNCTION argument that the engine invokes per entry/member. Because that function can navigate or consume the streamed input, they must NOT be blanket-grounded (that would over-accept a body that consumes the stream through the callback). They fall through to the conservative default (NotStreamable). Kept separate from the grounded map/array grounding arm in . (The fn: higher-order functions — fold-left/right, filter, for-each, for-each-pair, sort, apply — are likewise left in the Unknown default and are not listed here since they are keyed by namespace, not this set.)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifySelectTransmit(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: xsl:sequence transmits the select's posture AND sweep unchanged.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifyCopyOf(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: xsl:copy-of makes a GROUNDED deep copy of the selected sequence: the result posture is Grounded (detached), the sweep is the select's sweep (reading it consumes the stream). A non-streamable select propagates.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.ClassifyGroundingSink(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltSequenceConstructor,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: §19.8: classify a GROUNDING SINK instruction — xsl:message / xsl:assert — whose content (and optional select / test) is evaluated but contributes NO node to the constructed result tree. Result posture is always GROUNDED; the sweep is the combined sweep of the test, select, and content. A non-streamable (roaming / free-ranging) test, select, or content STILL propagates (the sink grounds streamed NODES, but it cannot rescue an expression that free-ranges or roams over the input — e.g. reverse(...), a consuming predicate filter). This distinguishes a striding xsl:sequence select="text()" inside a message (consumed for the message, grounded away) from the same instruction in a for-each body (which leaks a striding node into the result and is not streamable).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamabilityClassifier.SelectOrContentSweep(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltSequenceConstructor,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingContext)
member.summary: Combined sweep of an instruction that offers a select XOR a content body.

§19.8.2: classify an xsl:map-entry / xsl:array-member as a GROUNDED stored value, rejecting when its key () or value (/) is a live streamed NODE sequence (Striding/Crawling) that cannot be captured without buffering (si-map-901/902). Mirrors the CapturesStreamedNodes guard on the expression-form map/array constructors. Grounded/atomized/climbing keys and values are storable.

member.summary: Combined sweep of a (possibly null) sequence-constructor body.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture.Grounded

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture.Striding
member.summary: A set of nodes at the same level, all descendants-or-self of the context (e.g. child-axis paths).

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture.Crawling
member.summary: Nodes on the descendant/descendant-or-self axis, possibly nested.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture.Climbing
member.summary: Nodes reached by moving up toward ancestors of the context node.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture.Roaming
member.summary: Nodes at arbitrary positions relative to the context (not streamable).

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Posture.Artistic

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Sweep.Motionless

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.Sweep.Consuming

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingPlan
member.summary: The single buffering decision for an XSLT instruction under streaming, derived from the §19.8 posture/sweep classification. This one decision is intended to SUPERSEDE the two divergent legacy detectors ( and ) — one classification driving one plan, with no in-template / document-level divergence.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingPlan.StreamInline
member.summary: Run the instruction directly against the live streaming reader — nothing needs to be materialised. Only ever chosen for a construct (§19.8.6). Streaming a non-streamable construct would produce the wrong output, so this plan is NEVER returned unless streamability is guaranteed.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingPlan.BufferMatchedSubtree
member.summary: Materialise the MATCHED element's subtree (the current streaming context node) and run the instruction against that buffered tree. Chosen for guaranteed-streamable constructs that nonetheless need the matched subtree whole — a snapshot(.) / copy-of(.) of the context item, or a body that re-traverses the matched node's descendants.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingPlan.BufferWholeInput
member.summary: Materialise the WHOLE input document and run the instruction non-streaming. The safety net for a construct that is NOT guaranteed-streamable but still navigates the streamed input (a roaming/free-ranging select, group-by, a crawling for-each select, an input-navigating operand in an absorbing position, …). Correct output, just not streamed.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingPlan.NotStreaming
member.summary: The instruction is not a streaming construct and does not navigate the streamed input — purely grounded work. Nothing to buffer and nothing to stream.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.StreamingPlanner
member.summary: Derives a single for an XSLT instruction from its §19.8 posture/sweep classification (via ), replacing the two legacy, independently-maintained buffer detectors with one posture-driven decision.

remarks.para: This is a Task 1.1 shadow component: it is additive and wired into nothing (Task 1.2 does the runtime wiring). The legacy detectors remain intact as the coverage contract.

The overriding correctness invariant: is only ever returned for a instruction. Under-buffering is a correctness bug (wrong output); over-buffering is only a performance loss, so when in doubt the safe buffer plan is preferred.

member.summary: Computes the single buffering decision for in the streaming environment , per the §19.8 derivation rules.
member.param: The XSLT instruction to plan.
The streaming context (context-item posture and streamed-scope flag).
member.returns: The single buffering plan that supersedes both legacy detectors.

member.summary: True when a guaranteed-streamable instruction needs the matched element's subtree materialised: it applies snapshot(.) / copy-of(.) of the context item, or re-traverses the matched subtree (an inner xsl:copy-of / xsl:for-each / xsl:iterate / xsl:apply-templates that reads the context node's children / descendants after the node is needed whole).

member.summary: True when applies snapshot(.) / copy-of(.) (or of a downward path off the context) anywhere in its tree — the operations that demand the matched subtree be buffered. Mirrors the legacy detector's ExpressionUsesSnapshot.

member.summary: True when evaluates relative to the matched element (the streaming context node): bare ., a relative downward path, or parenthesised / simple-map / snapshot forms of those. Absolute paths and grounded refs do not. Mirrors the legacy detector's TouchesMatchedSubtree.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.Streamability.UsageClassifier.ClassifyContextItemUsage(System.Boolean)
member.summary: The §19.6/§19.7 usage a streamable for-each imposes on each matched context item ., driving the materialize-vs-atomize dispatch decision. When the for-each select explicitly atomizes the item (a fn:data(...) wrapper — ), the item is : the dispatch delivers the atomized value (a bare xsl:copy then copies the atomic as text — si-copy-002). Otherwise the matched item is : the dispatch delivers the real node (already materialized on the snapshot), which every body — value-of, copy-of, axis navigation — consumes correctly. The body does not refine this: the atom-vs-node signal is the select's atomization alone.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamabilityChecker
member.summary: Static streamability checker for XSLT 3.0 (section 19). Detects non-streamable expressions in streaming contexts and raises XTSE3430. This is a conservative checker: it detects common non-streamable patterns but does not implement the full posture/sweep classification from the spec.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamabilityChecker.MotionlessInspectionFunctions
member.summary: #143 Phase 2 — the single canonical set of "motionless node-inspection" function local names: functions to which passing the streamed context item (.) or a streamed parameter reads only node identity/name/count/existence WITHOUT consuming child content, so the reference inside the argument is motionless (does not raise XTSE3430). This replaces three previously-triplicated inline lists that had drifted apart (the widest of the three is used as the reconciled canonical membership). Kept aligned with the classifier's NodeProperty / Boolean / CurrentGroup roles; position()/last() are deliberately EXCLUDED (they are positional/free-ranging and handled separately).
Checks the body of an xsl:source-document streamable="yes" instruction. Throws XsltException with XTSE3430 if the body contains non-streamable expressions.
Checks a template body used in a streamable mode. Throws XsltException with XTSE3430 if the body contains non-streamable expressions.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.RequiresWholeInputBuffer(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltSequenceConstructor)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.IterateConsumesInput(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True when an xsl:iterate select navigates the input document (a path, or a function call wrapping a path such as outermost(.//x)) and therefore cannot be satisfied by the document-level streaming pass. member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.AttributesNavigateInput(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{PhoenixmlDb.Core.QName,PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltAttributeValueTemplate})

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.BodyNavigatesInput(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltSequenceConstructor)
member.summary: Broad test: does any instruction in read the input document? Used for xsl:on-empty / xsl:on-non-empty content, whose position has no document-level streaming dispatch — so even a bare downward path there cannot stream and must run buffered. A grounded body (literals / variables / ranges, no input navigation) stays on the streaming path. (#143)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.NavigatesInput(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True when reads the streamed input document directly — i.e. it contains a path / axis step or a bare context-item reference somewhere in its tree. An iterate select built purely from grounded operands (literals, ranges, variable references, and functions/operators over those — e.g. tail($words) or 1 to 200) iterates an already-materialized value and stays on the streaming path. A select that navigates the input (account/transaction, /*/transaction, outermost(.//gml:posList), descendant::x) cannot be satisfied at the document level and forces whole-input buffering.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.SelectReferencesContextAccumulator(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True when contains a call to an absorbing aggregation / reduction function anywhere in its tree whose operand navigates the input, where that call has no usable document-level streaming dispatch and would otherwise fold the empty synthetic document node. Such a call forces whole-input buffering. The call may be nested inside wrapping functions (round(sum(…)), format-number(avg(…), …), xs:integer(round(sum(…)))) or boolean connectives, so the whole select tree is walked. An aggregation over a grounded sequence (literals, variables, ranges) stays on the streaming path.
member.remarks:
Two function families are matched, distinguished by their streaming support:
No watcher at all — fold-left/fold-right (higher-order), and the absorbing predicates boolean/not/exists/empty plus the cardinality functions one-or-more/exactly-one/zero-or-one. These are never registered by , so ANY input-navigating operand falls to the empty-doc path. We buffer whenever the operand navigates the input.
Watcher-backed aggregations — sum/count/avg/ max/min/string-join. The streaming pass handles these whenever the operand is a single — either via a StreamWatcher (sum(//PRICE)) or via direct document-level path streaming, INCLUDING paths whose final step is a computed value or function call (sum(account/transaction/(@value*2)), sum(account/transaction/abs(@value)), max(.../PUB-DATE/xs:date(.))). We must NOT steal any of those — buffering a large input there would time out. So we buffer ONLY when the operand navigates the input AND is a COMPOSITE (non-path) shape the streaming pass cannot drive: a parenthesised sequence mixing paths and literals (sum((path, 31, 32))), a simple-map cast chain (sum(path!xs:decimal(.))), a FLWOR (sum(for $d in … return …)), a union (count(a | b)), or a function-wrapped operand (count(remove(path, 3))). See .
member.summary: True when evaluates accumulator-after() / accumulator-before() against the CONTEXT node — a bare call, or one wrapped only in arithmetic / a comma sequence / a filter / another function's arguments (i.e. NOT reached through a downward navigation step). At the document level (a match="/" template body or an xsl:source-document body) the context node is the principal source tree's root, so accumulator-after('x') there needs the accumulator value AFTER the whole tree has been consumed — a value not yet known at the document node's start event in a single forward pass (it folds to the initial value, e.g. <out>0</out> instead of 3). Route to the whole-input buffer, where PreComputeAccumulatorsAsync walks the full tree and returns the correct after-value. A call reached through a downward step (foo/accumulator-after('x')) evaluates against a descendant while striding and is left on the streaming path. (attr/mode mode-1107a/c)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.CollationArgNavigatesInput(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.FunctionCallExpression)
member.summary:
True when is an fn:-namespace function that takes a collation URI as a trailing argument AND that collation argument navigates the streamed input. The recognised functions and their collation-argument position (0-based):
distinct-values(seq, collation) — arg 1
index-of(seq, search, collation) — arg 2
max(seq, collation) / min(seq, collation) — arg 1
compare(a, b, collation) — arg 2; deep-equal(a, b, collation) — arg 2
Only the collation argument is inspected here (the data arguments are handled by the absorbing-classification above). A collation argument that does not navigate the input (a literal URI, a variable, or absent) is left on the streaming path.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.ClassifyAbsorbing(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.FunctionCallExpression)
member.summary: Classifies an fn:-namespace function call by its absorbing-aggregation family. See for why the two families are gated differently.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.SelectNavigatesViaClimbingAxis(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True when the selected nodes are reached by a NON-downward final step — an attribute or namespace node, or a climbing axis (parent / ancestor[-or-self] / preceding[-sibling]). Forward streaming only descends, so once the reader has passed a node it cannot go back to copy its attributes or ancestors; a copy-of / value-of / sequence selecting such nodes streams to the wrong value (si-copy-of-003: copy-of of account/transaction[@value lt 0]/@value into an attribute(*)* variable raised XTTE0570). Route to the whole-input buffer. A downward path (child / descendant[-or-self] / self) stays streaming. Wrapping simple-map / filter / single-item-sequence is peeled to the node-producing step. (#143)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.SelectCopiesWholeContextItem(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True when is (or, after peeling a wrapping single-item sequence / filter, resolves to) a snapshot(.) / copy-of(.) — or the zero-argument snapshot() / copy-of(), which default to the context item — whose argument is the BARE context item. At the xsl:source-document body / match="/" document level the context item is the document node, so this copies the WHOLE streamed input. There is no per-node streaming dispatch for a whole-document copy: the select evaluates against the synthetic empty document node and silently yields nothing (sf-copy-of-011 / sf-snapshot-0311 dropped the copied BOOKLIST, emitting only the surrounding grounded <head/><tail/>). Route to the whole-input buffer so the copy runs against the real document root. This is deliberately NARROW — only the bare context item qualifies; a copy-of(downward/path) stays on the streaming Snapshot-watcher path (buffering a large input would time out). (#143)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.SelectUsesGenericNodeTest(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True when is a path with any step using the generic node() kind test (a whose Kind is ), e.g. //node()[name() = $param]. The streaming for-each subscription matches element name / kind patterns, not the any-node-kind test, so such a select has no forward-pass dispatch and folds to empty. A name test (//*, //record) or a typed kind test (element(), text()) stays streaming. Wrapping filter / single-item sequence is peeled to the path. (#143)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.SelectNavigatesViaFunctionOrComposite(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True when an xsl:apply-templates select navigates the input through a FUNCTION call or other composite rather than a bare downward path — e.g. copy-of(outermost(//p))[pred] or snapshot(…). apply-templates dispatch streams only off a path it can match per node; a function-wrapped select evaluates against the synthetic empty node and applies templates to nothing, so it must run buffered. A bare path / context item (peeling a wrapping filter / single-item sequence) stays streaming. (#143)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.IsBarePathOperand(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary: True when is a single — the shape the streaming pass already drives directly off the live reader for a watcher-backed aggregation, whether or not the scanner registers a watcher for it. This deliberately accepts paths with computed or function-call final steps (account/transaction/(@value*2), account/transaction/abs(@value), .../PUB-DATE/xs:date(.)): those stream correctly today and must NOT be diverted to whole-input buffering (which on a large input would time out). A bare context-item reference is likewise left on the streaming path. Everything else — parenthesised sequences, simple-maps, FLWORs, unions, function-wrapped operands — is a composite the streaming pass can't satisfy at the document level, so it must be buffered.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.SelectNavigatesViaUnstreamableOperator(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryExpression)
member.summary:
True when is (or, after peeling a wrapping simple-map / filter, resolves to) an EXPRESSION OPERATOR node whose operand navigates the streamed input but which the document-level streaming pass cannot drive — so evaluating the select against the synthetic empty document node would drop the navigating operand or compute the wrong result. Such a shape forces whole-input buffering. The matched operators:
treat as / instance of / castable as ( / / ): the path operand evaluates to empty against the synthetic node, so (.//node()) instance of element()* returns the wrong boolean and (EXPR treat as T+) raises a spurious empty-cardinality error.
union / except / intersect (): a navigating operand on either side is dropped.
a square-array constructor [ … ] () over a navigating member.
a comma sequence (A, B) (, two or more items) mixing a navigating operand with grounded operands — the navigating side is dropped, leaving only the grounded items ((copy-of(//ITEM/PRICE), $insertion) emits just $insertion).
A BARE path / context-item operand (the shape the watcher dispatch already streams, e.g. copy-of(//ITEM), //x ! string(.)) is NOT matched — the helper only fires for the operator wrappers above, leaving plain streaming selects untouched.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.StreamingSubtreeBufferDetector.RequiresSubtreeBufferForAbsorbingFunctions(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltSequenceConstructor,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{System.ValueTuple{PhoenixmlDb.Core.QName,System.Int32},PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltFunction})

The XPath text begins inside an attribute value; the value's start position is computed from the attribute's plus the attribute name length and the =" delimiter (3 chars).

remarks.para: Line offset (D5): XPaths can span multiple lines (rare but legal). Line N within the XPath maps to file line (attr-line + N - 1). Column on line 1 of the XPath gets the value's start column added; subsequent lines start at column 1 of the file (no offset), which matches XML attribute-value continuation.

Column conventions: ANTLR (used by the XQuery parser) reports columns 0-based; reports them 1-based. We treat the stored on parsed expressions as ANTLR's 0-based form and add the 1-based attribute-value start column directly — the off-by-one cancels out for line-1 columns since ANTLR's "first character" is 0 while the attribute value's "first character" is at 1-based column N.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltException
member.summary: Represents an error that occurred during XSLT stylesheet compilation or transformation.

remarks.para: XsltException is thrown for both compile-time errors (malformed XSLT, invalid attribute values, unresolved imports) and runtime errors (type mismatches, failed assertions, dynamic evaluation errors). Check to determine where in the stylesheet the error originated.

When an error occurs during transformation, the contains a description of the XSLT error condition (e.g., XTDE0540 for conflicting xsl:result-document URIs), and pinpoints the stylesheet instruction that caused the failure.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltException.Location
member.summary: Gets the source location in the XSLT stylesheet where the error occurred, or null if the location is not available.
member.remarks: The location includes the line number and column number within the stylesheet, which is useful for diagnostic messages and IDE integration.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltException.ErrorCode
member.summary: The W3C error code this exception reports — XTDE0640, XPST0008, XTSE0010 — or null when the message carries none.

remarks.para: Derived from the message, because that is where 454 of this engine's 577 throw sites already put it: every one writes "CODE: description". Without this property the only way to ask "which error is this?" was to search the message text, and the engine did exactly that in seven places — including a deferral guard reading ex.Message.Contains("XTDE3400"), which would also have matched an error that merely quoted the code in its prose.
Prefer ErrorCode == "XTDE0640" to any test against : message text is for humans and changes freely; the code is the contract.

A deferred error must not be converted into "variable not bound" by the XQuery variable fallback: the variable *is* bound, its initializer failed.

member.summary: Sentinel stamped on of a COPIED DOCUMENT node whose source document had NO base URI (dm:base-uri = ()). member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.TcOpenElement(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.TreeConstructor,System.String,System.String)

The frame stays open (and stays active) through content; namespaces, attributes, and any prefix fixup are applied at before the frame is sealed.

Applies the string path's finalized namespace declarations and (deduplicated, last-wins) attributes to the still-open frame, mirrors any post-content prefix fixup, preserves an xsl:copy source base URI, then ends the element. member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.TypedBodyState
member.summary: Construction state saved on entry to an as=-typed sequence-constructor body, restored on exit. See .

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.ItemStarSequenceType
member.summary: Establishes the construction context shared by every as=-typed body — the seams behind xsl:variable, xsl:param, xsl:with-param, a parameter's default value, xsl:function and a typed template.
member.remarks:
These seams each grew their own save/reset/restore block, and they diverged. Every one of the five capture bugs found while unblocking XSpec was a field one seam handled and another did not:
_documentNodeDepth — variable had it, param/with-param/default did not, so an xsl:attribute inside as="attribute()*" raised a spurious XTDE0420.
_collectTextAsSequenceItems — variable had it, function did not, so a typed function returned a string where the caller declared node()* (XTTE0780).
_outputLogicalStart — variable had it, function did not, so a nested flush truncated the caller's buffer and crashed with ArgumentOutOfRangeException.
Centralising the context makes that class of divergence unrepresentable. Result ASSEMBLY stays per-seam: each genuinely differs in how it turns the captured channels into a value, and unifying that is a separate change.
A typed body constructs a SEQUENCE, not a temporary tree (XSLT 3.0 §9.3), so the document depth is neutralized — except for as="document-node()", whose body really is wrapped in a document node and must keep the guard armed.
member.summary: The default return type of an xsl:function that declares no as=: item()* (XSLT 3.0 §10.3).

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext._streamingOutputSink
member.summary: Optional external sink for incremental streaming output. When non-null, the calls at each safe event boundary to flush here and reset its length to zero, bounding peak memory for large streamed transforms. The sink is only meaningful when the context is driving a streaming transform; non-streaming callers leave it null.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.AsBodyCapture.ConsumedTo
member.summary: For each accumulator item, the output offset it consumed UP TO. Normally equal to its entry — the item contributed no serialized output.
member.remarks:
WriteTextItem deliberately writes text to BOTH the accumulator and _output inside a function body, so text and literal result elements keep their source order when the two are woven back together. The weave assumed they were disjoint: it inserted the item at its recorded offset and then emitted the rest of the output, which re-emitted the very same text. A template declared as="text()" returned TWO items — one TextNodeItem and one String, identical content — and failed XTTE0505.
Recording the end offset lets the weave skip the region an item already covers.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.AsBodyCapture.AttrDepthAtStart

member.remarks: Distinguishes "an element started OUTSIDE this template is still collecting its attributes" from "the body itself started an element". Only the first case means a copied attribute is part of the template's RETURN VALUE rather than content of an element the body is building. Without the distinction a typed template that copies an attribute silently contributed it to the caller's element and returned nothing.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.InTypedAsBodyAccumulator

Mirrors the guard.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.EvaluateBodyContentToValueAsync(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltSequenceConstructor)
member.summary:
Evaluates the body content of an xsl:param / xsl:with-param (when no `select` attribute is present) into a typed value, preserving xsl:sequence-emitted items.
The naive path (write to output buffer, then atomize the text) destroys typed items: an xsl:sequence emitting a document-node would serialize to text, then the text would be wrapped as XsUntypedAtomic, then bound to the parameter. Downstream code expecting `as="document-node()"` to preserve the doc-node would see XsUntypedAtomic and fail XPTY0020 on axis steps. Found in Docbook TNG fp:run-transforms's xsl:next-iteration with-param="document"; same shape as the xsl:variable accumulator-isolation fix earlier.
Strategy: install a fresh sequence accumulator around the body. xsl:sequence inside the body appends items to it; literal text falls through to the output buffer. After execution, prefer the accumulator items when present (they retain type), otherwise fall back to the output text wrapped as untyped atomic.

member.summary: XSLT 3.0: when a called template makes the context item absent (xsl:context-item use="absent"), the current group and current grouping key are absent too, so current-group()/current-grouping-key() must raise XTDE1061/XTDE1071 rather than leak the caller's group (si-fork-113/114). Shadows both grouping pseudo-variables with null in the callee scope; the caller's group is restored when that scope pops. Only called on the context-absent invocation path — a normal call-template retains the focus and correctly keeps the current group visible.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.OwningConstructIsGuaranteedStreamable
member.summary:
#143 Task 1.3 — the guaranteed-streamable invariant guard. Returns true when the construct that OWNS the current streaming execution (the matched streaming template whose body is being run against the live reader) is classified guaranteed-streamable per §19.8.6. Such a construct must be STREAMED or BUFFERED by StreamingPlanner.Plan — it must NEVER silently collapse to the built-in text-only copy (element structure lost) or be evaluated against the synthetic empty document node (empty output). The two sinks consult this to assert-loudly (Debug) / route-to-buffering (Release) instead of emitting the collapse.
Conservatism: the guard is armed ONLY under an active streaming execution with a matched current template whose body is available to classify. A node that legitimately reaches the built-in text-only copy with NO guaranteed-streamable owning construct (a genuinely unmatched node in a non-streaming pass, or an owning body that is itself not guaranteed-streamable) returns false and takes the normal path. This never fires on the text/attribute/atomic copy of leaf content inside a legitimately-streamed body — the owning-construct classification is the same guaranteed-streamable body in both the correct (streamed/buffered, never reaching here) and regressed (reaching here) cases, so the guard is triggered strictly by REACHING a sink that a guaranteed-streamable construct must not.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.DescribeOwningConstruct
member.summary: #143 Task 1.3 — names the owning construct for the invariant diagnostic. Best-effort: the current template's match pattern text plus the first structural instruction of its body, so a tripped assert points at the exact stylesheet shape (e.g. the 013 family).

member.summary: #143 Task 1.3 — Release safety net for a guaranteed-streamable construct that reached a silent sink. Rather than the structure-losing text-only copy (or an empty emission), this preserves the node's full structure by deep-copying its buffered subtree — the correct, never-collapsed output. Under an active streaming reader the subtree is materialised from the live reader (identical contract to the snapshot()/copy-of()/deep-copy streaming paths); otherwise the node is already a fully-populated tree and is serialized directly. This is a backstop only: Task 1.2's StreamingPlanner.Plan dispatch routes such constructs before they ever reach here, so in a non-regressed engine this method is unreachable.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.GroupByAccumulator
member.summary: Equality on group-adjacent keys. A composite key (composite="yes") is a SEQUENCE of atomic values (e.g. 007's (year, week)) surfaced as an array; equality is member-wise so two distinct tuples that happen to string-concatenate alike are still separated. Single atomic keys fall back to value-then-string comparison.

Accumulates xsl:for-each-group group-by members into groups, holding the whole of the grouping semantics in one place: collation, composite keys, sequence-valued keys (the item joins one group per value), an empty-sequence key (the item joins none), a key sequence with duplicates (the item joins each group once), numeric cross-type promotion so 1.0 and 1 group together, and first-appearance group order.
member.remarks:
Shared by the buffered path, which feeds it items from an evaluated select, and by the streaming path, which feeds it members materialized off the reader. Both must agree — group-by is far too subtle to implement twice, and this engine has already paid for letting two seams reimplement one contract.
Key EVALUATION stays with the callers: they differ in what context they push (buffered knows the population size up front, streaming does not), and only the accumulation itself is common.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.IsUntypedRtfFlipByteParitySafe(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{PhoenixmlDb.Core.NodeId},PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.TreeConstructor)
member.summary:
SP-C slice 3 scope guard: returns false when the constructor's fragment would NOT reparse byte-identically under the legacy serialize-then-reparse reference, so the flip must fall back to the RTF. Two Task-6 model differences are excluded:
Preserved copy-source base URI: any node carrying CopySourceBaseUri (or an entity BaseUri) — the plain untyped-RTF serialize path emits no base sentinel, so the reparse would recover null there.
Inherited namespace over-declaration: any element with a non-empty in-scope namespace set that has an element child — the reparse records the child's FULL in-scope set as its namespace declarations, where the constructor records only local ones.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.BuildUntypedRtfFlipDocument(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{PhoenixmlDb.Core.NodeId},System.String)
member.summary: SP-C slice 3: builds the delivered document node for a fully node-native untyped RTF body from the constructor's fragment roots, byte-identical to what would produce by serialize-then-reparse.
member.remarks:
The reparse takes one of two shapes, which this mirrors exactly:
Non-wrapped (XmlDocument.LoadXml(content) succeeds — content is a single well-formed root element with only whitespace/comment/PI misc around it): ConvertToXdm DROPS document-level text nodes (which can only be whitespace, else LoadXml would have failed). We detect this shape as "exactly one element root and every text root is whitespace-only" and omit those whitespace text roots from the children.
Wrapped (LoadXml fails — a fragment: multiple element roots, or non-whitespace text at the top level): the reparse wraps in _rtf_root_ and reparents ALL its children (text included) onto the document. We keep every root.
The document string value is the concatenation of the kept children's string values, which matches the reparse in both shapes (the non-wrapped reparse uses DocumentElement.InnerText — equal to the sole element's string value once the dropped whitespace is excluded).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.UntypedRtfFlipBlocked(PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Ast.XsltSequenceConstructor)

Blocks copies of source nodes (xsl:copy / xsl:copy-of) and template dispatch that may copy out of view (xsl:apply-templates / call-template / apply-imports / next-match) — these reroute base-URI preservation off the legacy accumulator+drain path — and any xml:base in the body, whose base-uri() resolution the reparse performs but the node build does not (all Task-6 base-uri work).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.DefaultXsltExecutionContext.EmitText(System.String)
member.summary: Writes text to the result tree, XML-escaping it — EXCEPT while it is being collected as an attribute VALUE, where it must be written verbatim.
member.remarks:
xsl:attribute with a sequence-constructor body runs that body into the ordinary output buffer and then takes the written span as the attribute's string value. Text escaped on the way in is therefore escaped a SECOND time when the finished value is serialized, so & came out as &amp; and a > written by xsl:text came out as &gt;.
This corrupts data silently: the attribute is well-formed, just wrong. XSpec's own compiler builds a select attribute this way — <xsl:attribute name="select"> around an XPath containing => — and the generated stylesheet then failed to parse with "token recognition error at: '&'", because the XPath lexer was handed a literal >.
The select and AVT forms of xsl:attribute were unaffected: they produce the value as a string directly and never route it through the escaping output path.

member.summary: Heuristic static cardinality check for an xsl:copy/@select expression in streaming context. Returns true ONLY for absolute paths (rooted at /) whose step shape provably yields more than one item — these can't be rescued by streaming subtree materialization the way relative paths can, so the runtime cardinality check would otherwise miss them (the absolute path evaluates against the synthetic empty document and silently returns zero items, masking XTTE3180). Relative paths (e.g. inner xsl:copy select="*") run against a real per-element context provided by the streaming subtree machinery and remain caught by the runtime nonNullItems.Count check.

The active streaming reader is still positioned before the document element (); walk it forward, materialize each top-level element subtree into the node store via (which leaves the reader on the subtree's EndElement), and serialize it into _output with copy-of semantics — reusing the same path a materialized element result would take. Top-level comments / processing-instructions are forwarded verbatim (child::node() selects them too); whitespace-only text between top-level nodes is dropped, matching the streamed-input strip-space default the subtree materializer applies.

member.param: Length of _output when the body started.
Whether an xsl:result-document had already claimed the principal output destination before the body ran.
member.remarks:
xsl:result-document returns the EMPTY SEQUENCE (XSLT 3.0 §26.1). One carrying an href is redirected into its own buffer, so it never lands here. One targeting the PRINCIPAL output has nowhere else to go — _output IS the principal result — so its content sits inside this body's capture window even though it is not the body's return value.
When the body claimed the principal output, return nothing and leave _output intact: the content is the principal result document and must still be serialized, but the body's return value is the empty sequence. XTDE1490 permits at most one such instruction per transformation and rejects a principal output that already has content, so the claimed region is exactly what the body wrote.

member.summary:
Converts a Uri to string, distinguishing two cases that look similar through .NET's API but need opposite handling:
Windows drive-letter path (e.g. C:\Users\…\file.xsl or C:/Users/…/file.xsl) — produces = "file" and as the path. We want the proper file URI form (file:///C:/Users/…) so doc() on the other side can recognize and read the file.
Non-standard scheme URI (e.g. d://tests/) — .NET on Linux mangles this to file:///d://tests/ via . We want to preserve .
The distinguishing pattern: a Windows drive path starts with one ASCII letter then ":" then "\" or "/". A non-standard scheme URI has a multi-char scheme name before "://", or uses a single-letter scheme followed by content that doesn't look like a drive path. The earlier "any colon means scheme mangling" heuristic caught both cases and broke doc() on Windows (Martin Honnen's report: localization-base-uri: C:/Users/marti/…/locale/ instead of file:///C:/…).

Shared because SIX call sites start a transform — TransformAsync and TransformRawAsync each reach an initial template via CallTemplateAsync and an initial mode via ApplyTemplatesAsync — and only TransformAsync passed any parameters. Every site in TransformRawAsync passed an empty list, so fn:transform's template-params and tunnel-params were silently dropped on every raw-delivery transform. The template ran and returned its default, which is why it looked like the options were unimplemented rather than undelivered.
The initial-MODE half is the one that matters in practice: XSpec compiles a scenario-level x:param under an x:context/@mode into template-params, so an entire suite ran with its parameters missing and terminated on the first assertion that read one.

member.summary:
At position in the already-escaped serialized string, determine the logical source character (the character as it appeared in the result tree, before XML escaping) and look it up in . This lets character maps key on the original character even though the serializer has already turned it into an entity reference — character maps are, per the serialization spec, applied to the pre-escaped characters, and their replacement is emitted verbatim (character-map-023/026). The logical character may be:
a predefined or numeric entity reference (<, 𘚠, …)
an astral character encoded as a UTF-16 surrogate pair (character-map-007)
an ordinary BMP character
On a hit, is advanced to the last consumed code unit (the caller's loop increment steps past it) and the replacement is returned. On a miss, is left unchanged so the caller emits the single code unit verbatim.

remarks.code: üss="üß" (name decomposed as well as the value)

The walk mirrors , which already had to make exactly this content-versus-markup distinction; keeping the two the same shape means a fix to the notion of "content" lands in both.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.IsDeferrableGlobalError(System.Exception)
member.summary: Initializes global parameters and variables in dependency order. This ensures that if param $x references $y, then $y is initialized first. Also handles transitive dependencies through function calls.
Decides whether an error raised while eagerly initializing a global variable may be deferred to the point of reference.
member.remarks: XSLT 3.0 §2.3.2 (Priming a Stylesheet) addresses this case directly: "If the initialization of any global variables or parameter depends on the context item, a dynamic error can occur if the context item is absent. It is implementation-defined whether this error occurs during priming of the stylesheet or subsequently when the variable is referenced; and it is implementation-defined whether the error occurs at all if the variable or parameter is never referenced." Deferring is therefore a choice, not a correction — but it is the choice Saxon makes, and real stylesheets rely on it. Priming eagerly would otherwise turn an unevaluatable declaration in an *imported* module into a fatal error for stylesheets that never reference it — the common case being <xsl:variable select="/"/> in a module imported by a stylesheet invoked with an initial template and no source document (XSpec's generated test stylesheets import the stylesheet under test and run it via a named template). Static errors are excluded: they are signalled whether or not the variable is used.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.InitialMatchSelectionVariable
member.summary: Binds externally-supplied parameter values over the stylesheet's globals.
member.remarks:
Only an xsl:param may be overridden this way. A name the stylesheet declares as a global xsl:variable is not a parameter at all, so a supplied value for it must have no effect (XSLT 3.0 §9.5) — the variable keeps its computed value.
These four call sites previously wrote EVERY supplied name straight into the global scope, so a caller could silently replace a variable's value with one of a different type, or with nothing. It stayed invisible for as long as fn:transform's stylesheet-params were not delivered at all. The moment they were, XSpec's global-override suite — whose entire purpose is asserting that an x:param never overrides an xsl:variable — stopped completing: the empty value it deliberately supplies replaced a variable declared as="xs:string", and the template returning it raised XTTE0505.
Declared parameters are applied here rather than skipped, because InitializeGlobalsInDependencyOrderAsync only binds the ones it evaluates; this pass is what guarantees a supplied value wins over a default regardless of evaluation order.
member.summary: The reserved name the initial match selection is bound to when it is supplied as a value. Namespaced so it cannot collide with a stylesheet's own global.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.ResolveGlobalRef(PhoenixmlDb.Core.QName,System.Collections.Generic.HashSet{PhoenixmlDb.Core.QName})
member.summary: Topologically sorts global declarations based on their dependencies.
Matches a variable REFERENCE against the set of declared global names, rescuing the case where the two carry different interned NamespaceIds for the same namespace URI.
member.remarks:
The reference is produced by the XPath parser and the declaration by the stylesheet parser. For an unprefixed name both sides use NamespaceId.None and the fast path matches; for a NAMESPACED name the ids can differ, the set lookup misses, and the dependency is never recorded. Nothing errors — the topological sort simply does not order the pair, so a global declared BEFORE the one it selects from is evaluated first and reads an unbound value. Observed as node kinds collapsing: comment() and element() came back as documents, attribute() as an empty string, namespace-node() as text.
See QNameNamespaces, which exists because this identity trap had already cost several separate bugs.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.CreateSourceReaderSettings
member.summary: Reader settings for parsing a principal source document.
member.remarks:
XSLT needs the internal DTD subset: entity references, and the attribute declarations that make id() and IDREF work. So DTDs are parsed rather than prohibited — but on two leashes, because parsing a DTD is where XML's two classic attacks live:
XmlResolver = null — no external DTD or entity is ever fetched, which is what closes XXE. Only the internal subset is honoured.
MaxCharactersFromEntities — caps total entity expansion, which is what closes the billion-laughs / quadratic-blowup family.
Both were already applied on the with-URI path; this exists so the without-URI path cannot drift from it again.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.ScopedOutputBuffer
member.summary: Scoped capture of writes to a via a length cursor, not via a string copy of the existing content.

remarks.para: Replaces the historical pattern:
with the cursor-based equivalent that allocates only the inner string and truncates the builder back to its saved length on disposal:
remarks.code: var saved = new XsltTransformEngine.ScopedOutputBuffer(_output); ... write inner content ... var inner = saved.GetWritten(); // O(M) alloc — the only one saved.Dispose(); // O(1) truncate
remarks.para: At N = 100 MB outer / M = 1 KB inner, the historical pattern allocates ~200 MB and copies the buffer twice; the cursor-based form allocates ~1 KB. This shows up most acutely in deeply-nested or many-iteration XSLT constructs over Dataverse-scale source documents.

Used as a regular struct (not using var ref-struct) so it can be stored in a try/finally block for code that wants to do the truncate after a possibly-throwing body — many of the existing save/restore sites have that shape.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.ScopedOutputBuffer.SavedLength
member.summary: The length of _output at the time this scope was opened.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.ScopedOutputBuffer.WrittenLength
member.summary: The number of characters written to _output since this scope was opened.
member.remarks: Clamped to be non-negative: the buffer can be shorter than _savedLength if it was Clear()ed underneath an open scope (e.g. an xsl:result-document or a finalize/flush path resets _output). In that case nothing this scope wrote survives, so the written length is 0 — without the clamp GetWritten would pass a negative count to StringBuilder.ToString and throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.ScopedOutputBuffer.GetWritten
member.summary: Returns the slice of _output written since this scope was opened, as a new string.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformEngine.ScopedOutputBuffer.Dispose
member.summary: Truncates _output back to its saved length, discarding anything written in this scope.
member.remarks: Only shrinks — never grows. If the buffer was already cleared/truncated below _savedLength (see ), setting Length = _savedLength would pad it back out with NUL characters; guarding avoids that corruption.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformOptions.InitialModeSelectValue
member.summary: The initial match selection supplied as a VALUE rather than as an expression to evaluate. Takes precedence over .
member.remarks: fn:transform's initial-match-selection option already holds real XDM items, and XSpec routes a context there whenever it is not a single node — so in practice this is a SEQUENCE, often of nodes. Turning such a value back into an XPath string cannot work: there is no expression that denotes an arbitrary existing node, and the previous conversion fell back to value.ToString(), which for a sequence is the CLR text "System.Object[]". That was then parsed as XPath and failed with "mismatched input ']'" — the empty predicate of Object[].

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.Xslt.Engine.XsltTransformOptions.InitialContextItem
member.summary: The context item to establish when an initial template is invoked with no source document.
member.remarks: fn:transform may be given both an initial-template and an initial-match-selection. The selection is not a source document - it can be an atomic value - so it cannot go through HasSourceDocument, but the named template still has to see it as the context item. Without this the engine pushed AbsentFocus and any template evaluating "." raised XPDY0002. XSpec relies on exactly that shape: its mirror templates are named entry points whose body is <xsl:sequence select="."/>.
